# teams agent blueprint create

Create an Agent 365 agent blueprint

## Usage

```
teams agent blueprint create [name] [options]
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description | Required |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| `name` | Agent name | No |

## Options

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--endpoint <url>` | [OPTIONAL] HTTPS messaging endpoint to register right away |
| `--permissions <scopes>` | [OPTIONAL] Comma-separated Microsoft Graph delegated scopes (e.g. Mail.ReadWrite,Chat.ReadWrite) to grant and make inheritable by every agent identity created from this blueprint. Falls back to `teams config` agent-default-permissions when omitted. |
| `--json` | [OPTIONAL] Output as JSON |
<!-- AUTOGENERATED:END -->

## Permission lists

`--permissions` and the `agent-default-permissions` config value accept
comma-separated or whitespace-separated scopes. Duplicate scopes are removed.
Quote the list to keep it together across shells:

```bash
teams agent blueprint create "My Agent" --permissions "Mail.ReadWrite Chat.ReadWrite"
```

Omitting `--permissions` uses the configured default. Passing `--permissions ""`
overrides that default with no optional Graph scopes; mandatory agent and
messaging permissions are still configured.
